definitions.explanation: Chewy fruit-flavoured candy made with gelatin, sold in bags at every convenience store. From German Gummi. (Also the name of a native shrub with small red edible berries, now rarely met.)

examples.japanese: ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧グミ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a new kind of gummy candy at the convenience store.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧グミ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{固|かた}い→固い：12090_katai⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{噛|か}み→噛む：01205_kamu⟧ごたえ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Hard gummies are popular these days, and more people enjoy their chewy texture.

notes:
From German Gummi (rubber, gum), via the gummy bears sold in Japan from the 1980s. Japanese convenience stores stock dozens of kinds, and new flavours are a regular topic on social media.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{果汁|かじゅう}→果汁：15335_kajuu⟧グミ: fruit-juice gummies
- ハードグミ: hard gummies
- グミキャンディー: gummy candy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ガム→ガム：00058_gamu⟧: chewing gum; chewed and not swallowed
- ⟦キャンディー→キャンディー：23081_kyandii⟧: candy; usually hard sweets
